title: Emergency procedures and evacuation
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Follow site-specific alarms, exits, assembly points and emergency communication
Identify personal authority limits and stop-work triggers
Document and escalate site incidents using factual, privacy-conscious records

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Purpose and competence
instruction.body: This lesson teaches the worker to follow site-specific alarms, exits, assembly points and emergency communication. Apply employer procedures, the site induction and the actual work order. This is general training, not authorisation to perform specialist rescue, hazardous-material response or medical treatment. The learner must identify limits of authority and explain when to stop and escalate.

instruction.heading: Prepare and confirm authority
instruction.body: Before work, identify the designated supervisor, site contact, emergency number, nearest safe exit, incident reporting channel and any worker-specific restrictions. Check the current site instructions rather than relying on a previous visit. Confirm that any required equipment and communications are available. If essential controls are missing, do not commence the affected activity.

instruction.heading: Safe operating procedure
instruction.body: Locate exits, fire doors, assembly points and emergency contacts during induction. On alarm, stop work, leave by the safe route and follow trained wardens. Do not re-enter for belongings. In Australia call 000 for immediate life-threatening emergencies; follow site instructions and communicate the exact location.

instruction.heading: Worked workplace example
instruction.body: An alarm activates while a cleaner is using powered equipment. They leave equipment only if safe to do so, evacuate, report to assembly and do not return until authorised.

instruction.heading: Communicate, record and resume
instruction.body: Communicate the location, hazard, people potentially affected, actions taken and assistance required. Record time and facts promptly without naming uninvolved clients or speculating about causes. Only resume after the responsible person confirms the hazard is controlled and the work plan is safe. For emergency procedures and evacuation, practise repeating the decision sequence under changed conditions.

instruction.heading: Common errors and corrective coaching
instruction.body: Common errors include continuing because the job is nearly finished, treating PPE as the only control, concealing near misses, improvising outside training, and sharing client information in unsecured messages. The assessor should ask the learner to identify the unsafe decision, select a stronger control, and document who can authorise resumption.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Before work, identify the designated supervisor, site contact, emergency number, nearest safe exit, incident reporting channel and any worker-specific restrictions.
Check the current site instructions rather than relying on a previous visit.
Confirm that required equipment and communications are available, and do not start the affected activity if essential controls are missing.
Locate exits, fire doors, assembly points and emergency contacts during induction.
On an alarm, stop work and leave by the safe route, leaving equipment only where that is secure.
Follow trained wardens, report to the assembly point, and do not return for belongings or until authorised.
For an immediate life-threatening emergency, call 000 and give the exact location, following site instructions.
Communicate the location, hazard, people affected, actions taken and assistance needed, and record times and facts without speculating about causes.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: Exits, fire doors, assembly points and emergency contacts are located during induction.
When the alarm sounds, the cleaner halts activity, exits via the marked route, and abandons kit only where doing so is secure.
The cleaner reports to the assembly point and does not return until authorised.
Immediate life-threatening emergencies are reported by calling 000, with the exact location given.
summary: Exits, fire doors, assembly points and emergency contacts are located during induction.
On an alarm, work stops and the cleaner leaves by the safe route, following trained wardens and not going back for belongings.
Immediate life-threatening emergencies are reported by calling 000 in Australia, with the exact location given and site instructions followed.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the first priority when emergency procedures and evacuation reveals an uncontrolled immediate danger?
options: Collect bags and equipment before leaving
Re-enter the building to finish the room once the alarm stops
Stay in place and wait for the client to say whether it is a drill
Stop work, leave by the safe route and go to the assembly point

knowledgeChecks.question: When can staff re-enter a building after an evacuation alarm?
options: Only when the responsible person authorises re-entry
When the supervisor sounds calm on the phone
Once the worker has checked the building personally

knowledgeChecks.question: What should an evacuation incident record capture instead of speculation about the cause?
options: The likely cause of the alarm, guessed from a smell and the name of the person who guessed it
Actions taken, times and people notified, kept separate from speculation about the cause
The names of everyone in the building at the time, whether involved or not
Only the worker's personal opinion of the incident and how they felt about the room
